problem: Use a fundamental vector product to determine which of the following integrals gives the surface area generated when the curve $x=1+{y}^{2}$ is rotated by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis for $y\in [-1,1].$

feedback.problem: Use a fundamental vector product to determine which of the following integrals gives the surface area generated when the curve $y=\frac{x}{x+1}$ is rotated by $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in [0,4].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $y=\frac{x}{x+1}\ge 0$ for all $x\in [0,4].$ The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨x,\,f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,(x,\theta )\in D\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x)=\frac{x}{x+1},$ and

$$
D={(x,\theta )\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi }.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂x},\,\frac{∂y}{∂x},\,\frac{∂z}{∂x}⟩=⟨1,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨0,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨f{f}^{′}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +f{f}^{′}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨f{f}^{′},\,-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖ & =\sqrt{(f{f}^{′})^{2}+(-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{f}^{2}({f}^{′})^{2}+{f}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\sqrt{{f}^{2}({f}^{′})^{2}+{f}^{2}} \\  & =f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={∬}_{D}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta \,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\cdot \theta \,{|}_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(x)=\frac{x}{x+1},$ we obtain ${f}^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}}.$ So, finally, we conclude that our expression for the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{x}{x+1}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{x}{x+1}\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{(x+1)^{4}}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
